issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for the subroutine 'set_pixel': the template and problem statement expect and call a symbol named 'set_pixel' (template defines the label 'set_pixel:' and main does 'call set_pixel'), but the solution defines the routine with the label '.set_pixel:' (leading dot). Because symbol names must match exactly in assembly, the call site in main ('call set_pixel') will not resolve to '.set_pixel', causing an unresolved symbol / incorrect call and preventing the program from correctly invoking the implemented routine.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the subroutine symbol name identical in both template and solution. Change the solution label from '.set_pixel:' to 'set_pixel:' so that 'call set_pixel' in main resolves correctly (or alternatively change the call sites to 'call .set_pixel' everywhere). Prefer changing the solution to 'set_pixel:' to match the problem statement and template; ensure any saved/restored registers and calling conventions remain unchanged.

issues.description: The exercise describes and the template stub uses the subroutine label 'set_pixel' (problem statement: 'set_pixel'; template: label 'set_pixel:' at template_repository/pixel.asm:37), but the solution defines the routine with the label '.set_pixel:' (solution_repository/pixel.asm:19). This leading-dot variant is a different identifier from 'set_pixel' and prevents a direct one-to-one mapping between the problem requirement, the template stub, and the reference implementation, causing students to be unable to directly locate or compare the implemented subroutine against the described/stubbed name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the subroutine identifier consistent across all artifacts. Rename the solution label from '.set_pixel:' to 'set_pixel:' in solution_repository/pixel.asm (and ensure any internal references match), so the exact identifier 'set_pixel' appears in problem_statement.md, the template, and the solution. Alternatively, if the leading-dot is intentional (assembler-local label convention), update the problem statement and template to document and use the same '.set_pixel' form, but the simpler fix is to remove the leading dot in the solution.
